steps.instruction: Strip about a centimeter from each wire end.
steps.done_looks_like: Two white wires lie apart with short copper ends exposed.

checks.text: Both wire ends show exposed copper

common_mistakes: Cutting or nicking the copper strands

steps.instruction: Twist the bare ends together to lock them.
steps.done_looks_like: The two white wires form one loop with copper ends twisted into a small join.

checks.text: There are two white wires joined
The bare copper ends are twisted together with no loose strands

common_mistakes: Only pushing ends together without twisting
Twisted join is loose with stray strands
Joining insulation instead of copper to copper

steps.instruction: Apply flux to the twisted join.
steps.done_looks_like: The twisted copper join looks wet in the middle of the white wire loop.

checks.text: The joined white wire is present
The twisted copper join is coated with flux

common_mistakes: Putting flux on the insulation instead of the copper join
Using so much flux it pools everywhere

steps.instruction: Solder the join until solder spreads along it.
steps.done_looks_like: The center join is covered with shiny silver solder joining the white wires.

checks.text: The white wire loop is present
Silver solder is present at the join
The solder has flowed through and around the join with no bare copper showing

common_mistakes: Solder blob sitting on top without flowing through
Overheating and melting the white insulation

steps.instruction: Slide heat-shrink sleeving over the soldered join.
steps.done_looks_like: A black tube covers the soldered join with white insulation visible on both sides.

checks.text: The black sleeve is centered over the join covering all solder

common_mistakes: Sleeve left away from the join
Sleeve not overlapping white insulation on both sides
Solder still exposed at one end of the sleeve

steps.instruction: Heat the sleeving until it shrinks tight.
steps.done_looks_like: The black sleeve is tight around the white wire forming a secure insulated join.

checks.text: The black sleeve is present over the join
The black sleeve is shrunken tight with no gaps

common_mistakes: Removing heat too soon leaving sleeve loose
Overheating and melting the white insulation
Sleeve moved off the join during heating
